transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has landed in China, where he'll stay for only about 24 hours.
Some high-stakes meetings with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin are
on the agenda.
NPR's Deepa Shivram reports this is Trump's second visit to China this year.
After meeting with allies in Manila, Trump is headed into major summits with adversaries.
Relations between the U.S. and China have cooled since last year, when Trump and Xi
met in South Korea amid an escalating trade war.
The two nations still share tension, though, over access to rare earths and AI chips.
The meeting between Trump and Xi is not expected to deliver much that is new, but their consistent
meetings this year help solidify a more stable relationship, analysts say.
Both leaders will meet again next month in Miami, where Trump is hosting the G20 summit.
Deepa Shivram, NPR News Shenzhen.
The Associated Press has called Alaska's Senate race for Democratic challenger Mary Peltola.
She's flipped the seat and defeated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan.
House Democrats are holding elections today for their new leadership in the next Congress.
Current House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has called for a briefing of intelligence
leaders on Capitol Hill.
And Pierre's Eric McDaniel reports this follows several high-profile tech outages in recent
days.
The company, so far the only declared candidate for Speaker of the House and the new Congress,
says that after flights went down and tech behemoths faltered, disrupting huge swaths
of the U.S. economy, it's time for some information from the Trump administration.
I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves
so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people
of the United States of America.
So far, the administration has not given any suggestions that the outage is the result
of malignant actors, Eric McDaniel, NPR News Washington.
Older adults are among the millions of people who've lost SNAP food aid in the past year.
That is after Republican lawmakers passed sweeping changes to the program.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports on what expanded work rules mean for one woman who retired
early.
Lisa Reese stopped working at 62 to help out family, including taking care of a granddaughter
to save on daycare costs, but she could barely get by as prices shot up this year, especially
her gas bill.
Oh my goodness, that went through the roof.
One of my bills was $500.
This summer, she was approved for $63 a month in food aid, but to get it under new work
rules, she volunteers 80 hours a month at a local food pantry.
The Trump administration says such requirements are cutting costs and tackling fraud.
Reese loves helping out, but...
I have arthritis in my hand real bad, high blood pressure, you name it.
She's not sure how long she can keep it up.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Capitol Heights, Maryland.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Officials with computer chip maker Invidia say they will not bring Jensen Huang back
as CEO.
Huang quit after admitting an affair last week.
It was reportedly with a woman who was a suspected spy for China.
New York Attorney General Letitia James has formally challenged efforts to remove her from
the Cornell rape investigation.
Opponents have submitted a revised petition.
From members station WAMC, Elias Guerra has more.
In a memo filed Monday in State Supreme Court, attorneys representing the attorney general
pushed back against a petition signed by five students accused of sexual assault in the
2024 incident at Cornell University.
The petition revolves around a social media post.
James wrote, saying, "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable."
The state's memo argues the petition still has flaws.
Namely, other defendants in the Jane Doe litigation were left out of the petition,
but could still be found criminally liable.
They also argued that since Jane Doe's case is in Tompkins County, the petition should
be filed there instead of Albany County.
For NPR News, I'm Elias Guerra.
Earlier today, the space probe Voyager 1 achieved an astonishing record.
NASA says it is now one full light day away from Earth.
That's about 16 billion miles, or the same amount of time as it takes light to travel
in 24 hours.
Voyager 1 is now the farthest away from Earth that any human-made object has ever traveled
in space, and it's still going.
Voyager 1 launched in 1977.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump lands in China for a 24-hour visit with meetings with Xi Jinping and Putin
AP calls Alaska Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola, defeating Dan Sullivan
House Democrats hold leadership elections; Hakeem Jeffries calls for intelligence briefing on tech outages
Lisa Reese, 62, struggles to keep SNAP food aid under new work rules requiring volunteer hours
Nvidia will not bring back Jensen Huang as CEO after he admitted an affair with suspected Chinese spy
New York AG Letitia James formally challenges removal from Cornell sexual assault litigation
Voyager 1 reaches one light day from Earth, the farthest human-made object ever traveled
